pull.title: guix: pass `--disable-wchar_t` to (non-GUI) libstdc++
pull.body:
Introduce a minimal variant of `linux-base-gcc`, and use it for non-GUI builds.

This saves roughly half a megabyte in binary size, in the non-GUI binaries:

| Binary | master (MB) | PR (MB) |
|---|---|---|
| bitcoin | 2.15 | 1.67 |
| bitcoin-cli | 8.20 | 7.72 |
| bitcoin-qt | 43.87 | 43.87 |
| bitcoin-tx | 4.93 | 4.45 |
| bitcoin-util | 4.52 | 4.04 |
| bitcoin-wallet | 9.26 | 8.77 |
| bitcoind | 17.75 | 17.27 |

See https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/libstdc++/manual/configure.html:

> `--enable-wchar_t[default]`
> Template specializations for the wchar_t type are required for wide
> character conversion support. Disabling wide character specializations
> may be expedient for initial porting efforts, but builds only a subset
> of what is required by ISO, and is not recommended. By default, this
> option is on. This option can change the library ABI.

> pass --disable-wchar_t to non-GUI GCC

Isn't `--disable-wchar_t` a `libstdc++` configure option rather than a GCC one?

> Isn't --disable-wchar_t a libstdc++ configure option rather than a GCC one?

Yes, and we are passing that option through GCC. I will make the commit message clearer.

> We can do instead:

Looking at that diff, maybe we could also define `BOOST_NO_CWCHAR`? I don't particularly mind how this is patched out. Feel free to submit something upstream, and we could switch to it, if this code isn't removed first (#35713).

I am mainly looking for Concept ACKs on the overall change, and primarily review of d890a9ecd50c9bcd069185258582c8bad3e62450 (which is shared between #25573). Happy to split that out if needed.

Concept ACK.

> Looking at that diff...

I retract my proposal. It was incorrect.

> ... maybe we could also define `BOOST_NO_CWCHAR`?

Boost does this [automagically](https://github.com/boostorg/config/blob/115e718e0fd72329e69fc776dac99811385d6f77/include/boost/config/stdlib/libstdcpp3.hpp#L20-L25):
```c++
#if !defined(_GLIBCPP_USE_WCHAR_T) && !defined(_GLIBCXX_USE_WCHAR_T)
#  define BOOST_NO_CWCHAR
#  define BOOST_NO_CWCTYPE
#  define BOOST_NO_STD_WSTRING
#  define BOOST_NO_STD_WSTREAMBUF
#endif
```

It might be worth checking for potential side effects of those macros on Boost.MultiIndex.

> I am mainly looking for Concept ACKs on the overall change, and primarily review of [d890a9e](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/d890a9ecd50c9bcd069185258582c8bad3e62450) (which is shared between #25573). Happy to split that out if needed.

In my opinion, splitting it out would help.

Rebased, and added another commit, that passes [`--with-libstdcxx-zoneinfo=no`](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/libstdc++/manual/configure.html):
> The choice OPTION=no will disable all code for loading time zone
> info from file or from the embedded static data, which means that
> only the "UTC" and "GMT" time zones are defined.
    
> Using OPTION=no results in a smaller library, so is suitable for
> systems that will never need to query the time zone database.
> This does not change the library ABI.

> In my opinion, splitting it out would help.

Split it into #36272.
Reworked a bit, and moved out of draft.
